candidates.name: Centro Atlántico de Arte Moderno
candidates.content: The former Banco de España building has been a modern art museum since 1989, housing a collection of about 2,500 works mainly from Europe, Africa and the Americas.

candidates.name: Castillo de la Luz
candidates.content: A 16th-century fortification that was built to fend off pirate attacks. Today it's surrounded by a rose garden and since the 1960s it houses a cultural centre - Fundación de Arte y Pensamiento Martín Chirino - and a shipping museu

candidates.name: Catedral de Santa Ana
candidates.content: Embodying several centuries of history, the cathedral can be seen from almost any point in the city centre. Building began in 1497, and went on for several centuries and as such it's built in many different styles - gothic, baroqu

candidates.name: Columbus house museum
candidates.content: The house where Columbus lived when his ships were repaired and improved for his first journey to the West Indies, at the time the house was the residence of the governor. It was remodeled in 1777 so it looks a bit different now a

candidates.name: Elder Museum of Science and Technology
candidates.alt: Museo Elder de la Ciencia y la Tecnología
candidates.content: Interactive science museum, with a planetarium, a space station replica and a 3D cinema. Most exhibitions have information in both Spanish and English. When you're in, you can also use the Internet computers there, so the entrance

candidates.name: Plaza de Santa Ana
candidates.content: The square in the front of the cathedral has eight statues out of green rock depicting dogs. It's also lined by other grand buildings: Casa Consistorial (old town hall), Casa Regental, and the Palacio Episcopal (bishop's palace).

candidates.name: Museo Néstor
candidates.content: Art museum displaying the works of Néstor Martín-Fernández de la Torre (1887 - 1938), one of the most famous painters of the Canary Islands.

candidates.name: Parque Santa Catalina
candidates.content: This is where most of the hot nightlife spots can be found. It's also pretty during the day, although it consists of little more than a few palm trees. There are small cafés next to the park and you can see elderly locals playing

candidates.name: Alfredo Kraus Auditorium
candidates.content: Concert and music hall with classical philharmonic performances and a building that's worth a visit on its own.

candidates.name: Ermita de San Antonio Abad
candidates.content: A former church built in 1757 on the site of a chapel where according to legend Columbus prayed before setting sail westwards. It is used as an exhibition space for the Centro Atlántico de Arte Moderno.

candidates.name: Museo Canario
candidates.content: Founded in 1879, this museum has the largest collections of objects from the island from the pre-Spanish era, with the oldest objects from about 500 BC. There are models of traditional houses, a replica of the Cueva Pintada cave i

candidates.name: Poema del Mar
candidates.content: Aquarium opened in 2018 with three different themes named jungle, reef-beach and deep ocean. The big aquarium can be watched from all sides and from the middle, and some of the highlights are big rays and sharks. There's a restaur

candidates.name: Casa-Museo Pérez Galdós
candidates.content: The birth house of Benito Pérez Galdós (1843-1920), one of the most famous Spanish 19th-century novelists, now a museum displaying his life and works.

candidates.name: Pueblo Canario
candidates.content: A reconstruction of a traditional village, designed by Néstor Martín Fernández de la Torre in 1937 and realized by his brother Miguel two years later. The village covering 3,500 m² is in the Doramas Park and is also a venue for di

candidates.name: Ermito de San Telmo
candidates.content: In Triana, at the end of the shopping street. A tiled kiosk houses a café, with tables and chairs below palms where you can take a break and watch people walking by, and the small San Telmo chapel.

candidates.name: Parque Doramas
candidates.content: Named after the Guanche hero Doramas, it's regarded as the most beautiful park in the city. In the present day it's part of the villa district of Ciudad Jardin.

candidates.name: Plaza de Espana
candidates.content: One of the traffic nodes of the city, right at Avenida Mes y López. The square has cafés popular with the younger upper class at nighttime.

candidates.name: Playa de Las Canteras
candidates.content: Almost 4 km in length, this beach is the very symbol of the city and its citizens. The northern section has golden sand and is above water most of the time. It is good for swimming with low tide, when the barrier emerges, stopping

candidates.name: Playa de Las Alcaravaneras
candidates.content: Beach right at the port, suitable for tanning rather than water activities.

candidates.name: Playa del Confital
candidates.content: Beach with volcanic rock surface, mostly used by locals. There are permanent beach chairs and a toilet.

candidates.name: Playa de la Laja
candidates.content: Beach with grey and brown-black fine sand surface to the southeast of the city, popular with surfers.

candidates.name: Auditorio Alfredo Kraus
candidates.content: The main venue for classical music and art, built in the 1990s after a design by Óscar Tusquets, next to Las Canteras beach. It's architecturally striking as well, with a huge window to the sea.

candidates.name: Teatro Pérez Galdós
candidates.content: The main theatre named after author Benito Pérez Galdós (1843-1920), the main representative of the literary style Spanish realism, who was born in the city. On the adjacent square there's a large monument dedicated to him.

candidates.name: Real Club de Golf de Las Palmas
candidates.content: 18-hole golf course.

candidates.name: UD Las Palmas
candidates.content: They were relegated in 2025 and now play soccer in Segunda División, the second tier. The stadium seats 32,400.

candidates.name: Las Palmeras
candidates.content: Golf course with six tennis fields.

candidates.name: Gran Canaria Arena
candidates.content: Basketball court and cultural venue.

candidates.name: Teatro Guiniguada
candidates.content: Cultural venue in an impressive palace built in 1938. Theatre, dance and music shows and film screenings take place here.

candidates.name: Bar San Remo
candidates.content: Cozy bar with indoor and outdoor seating, pool and darts.

candidates.name: Chester Lounge & Bar
candidates.content: Large nightclub and bar.

candidates.name: NYC TAXI RockBar
candidates.content: Bar where blues and rock music is played. Also serves hamburgers and sandwiches.

candidates.name: La Azotea de Benito
candidates.content: Cocktail bar on the roof of a shopping mall.

candidates.name: Ginger
candidates.content: Cocktail bar.

candidates.name: Bodegón Pachichi
candidates.content: A classic for cheap drinks, and a favourite with locals.

candidates.name: La Coqueta de Cano
candidates.content: Fabulous little tavern for tapas. Charming, pleasant, a meeting point, endearing and... as if the name indicates: Flirtatious. Emblematic and charming terrace.

candidates.name: La Travesia de Triana
candidates.content: Great tapas bar with flair, larger selection of wines than in many other tapas bars. The grilled octopus or the fried black pudding are real highlights. Great food and amazing atmosphere! Also a good sign to be swarmed by locals w

candidates.name: Restaurante Que leche!
candidates.content: Exquisite treatment, careful and delicious food, excellently presented. A small place with personal service. The broken eggs and the aguachile to be loved. Attentive service and great local wines. Reservation for the dinner is rec

candidates.name: Tasca Siete Viejas
candidates.content: A lovely tapas bar. The food is incredible, the waiter so lovely and helpful. The chicken salad, the asparagus with truffle and Parmesan, the grilled cheese and the potatoes are amazing. The staff is very kind and the bar has a lo

candidates.name: Restaurante Samoa
candidates.content: A favourite of the locals, for good solid Spanish food with appropriate (not too high) prices. Top Spanish tapas and home made local cuisine. A super homey place, the waiters are super attentive and very friendly.

candidates.name: Restaurante Ons
candidates.content: Spectacular second courses and giant portions. Generous, cordial, emotional service. The food is beautifully presented and very delicious. Highly recommend is the potato salad with shrimps. Less touristic place with really good si

candidates.name: Restaurante Tabla Caliente
candidates.content: A different place to eat very well. They make the food in front of you, with care and professionalism. Very friendly, they recommend you according to your tastes. A lovely local restaurant.

candidates.name: Bodegón Pachichi
candidates.content: A pleasant place to eat typical Canarian tapas and have a good time. Quality local gastronomy. Good vibes.

candidates.name: Sakura City
candidates.content: Good quality, well-priced Japanese & Asian cuisine. Great for a little something different. Perfect for group or family dinning out. Seated buffet all-you-can-eat menu when dinning in. Various dishes selection for take-away or del

candidates.name: La Candella
candidates.content: Good wood-fired pizzas to go or to eat in.

candidates.name: Camino al Jamonal
candidates.content: Really good jamón and ibérico restaurant. The treatment is very friendly, the place charming and the food exceptional. It is hard to find a restaurant of this quality on the island. The restaurant has few tables so you have to boo

candidates.name: Restaurante Marisquería Rías Bajas
candidates.content: Excellent Spanish food. Very tasty dishes, unique service and a cozy place. Highlighted are the quality of its products, the sincerity and professionalism of its employees. Central location with terrace.

candidates.name: Centro Comercial Las Arenas
candidates.content: The largest shopping mall in the city, featuring a big Carrefour hypermarket. Reportedly very noisy.

candidates.name: Mercado Central
candidates.content: The central market has a large selection of fish and seafood.

candidates.name: Mercado de Vegueta
candidates.content: Founded in 1787 it's the oldest market. It's a particularly good place to buy fresh fruit, most of which has been grown on the Canary Islands.

december.text: Christmas: Christmas is considerably warmer than where most visitors come from, and it's common to throw parties on Las Canteras beach.
